findings.title: Denial as re-occlusion
findings.claim: Within the pericope's cover-and-disclosure movement, 92:9's denial can be heard as actively covering a good that has become perceptible.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the verb that declares al-husna false; the night and covering occurrences in 92:1 and the day and disclosure occurrences in 92:2 supply alternating withdrawal and appearance. Their contact makes the fixed object of denial something that can be disclosed and then covered again, while the ordinary judgment of falsehood remains available.
findings.reader_payoff: Denial becomes perceptible as an overlay placed on an available good, rather than only as a settled negative proposition.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains 've en güzeli yalanlarsa'. The packet also leaves open the ordinary propositional rejection after disclosure; this finding does not assert a surah-wide image or replace the clause's plain sense.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic anchors verify surface contact, but HFT segmentation, roles, and the unresolved context branches are attributed nominations. The in-pericope contact is sufficiently explicit for a qualified contextual finding.

findings.containment: The primary reading remains 've en güzeli yalanlarsa'. The packet leaves open the alternative in which the diversity of striving is neutral and the clause simply names one rejected good; no claim about the surah's thesis is made.

findings.title: A substitute that fails the test
findings.claim: Between claimed self-sufficiency and its later failure, denial participates in a reversal in which reliance displaced from al-husna onto wealth is exposed as unable to suffice.
findings.mechanism: The focus's ordinary denial of the named good meets the self-sufficiency claim in 92:8 and the later question of what wealth can avail at the fall in 92:11. The repeated sufficiency field, the material substitute of wealth, and the falling event make the rejected good and the trusted substitute part of one reversal, while the ordinary warning about greed remains live.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the focus as part of an expectation dynamic: a declared independence redirects reliance, and wealth later becomes the provision that fails the test.
findings.containment: The primary reading remains 've en güzeli yalanlarsa'. The packet also allows a straightforward warning about stinginess and wealth without a deliberate lexical rebound; this finding does not claim that the reversal is the sole interpretation.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic anchors are supplied, but the HFT roles and unresolved branches are attributed, and the rebound from the rejected good to wealth is explicitly an inference.
